card.title: Mac1 diffuse scattering East-West
card.summary: Two teams at CHESS and ALS measured 3D diffuse scattering maps from Mac1 crystals and compared them with a new noise-aware metric, CC_lim. The maps agreed within experimental error across teams and visits, and humidity, crystal number, X-ray dose and crystal size set the data quality.

paper.title: Iterating diffuse scattering protocols in parallel leads to reproducible, high-quality data from Mac1
paper.authors: Zielinski K, Meisburger S, Lu K, Bassim V, Holton J, Fraser JS, Ando N

nodes.title: QUE - Are 3D diffuse scattering maps reproducible across independent teams, beamlines and visits?
nodes.desc: Earlier agreement tests used one group's data from one facility. The diffuse signal is weak and sensitive to beamline, sample handling and processing.

nodes.title: QUE - Do the Mac1 diffuse maps contain features suitable for modeling correlated motion?
nodes.desc: Asks whether the maps show halos and cloudy patterns at a quality comparable to earlier lysozyme datasets.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Separating isotropic and anisotropic contributions'; 'Comparing data quality', last paragraph

nodes.title: QUE - How can agreement between two diffuse datasets be judged against their noise?
nodes.desc: A single correlation coefficient over a broad resolution range is dominated by strong features and cannot show where agreement breaks down.
nodes.loc: Introduction, paragraph 3; Results: 'Comparing data quality and consistency across datasets'

nodes.title: QUE - Which experimental variables most limit diffuse data quality and agreement?
nodes.desc: Retrospective analysis of less ideal datasets from the optimization process: crystal number, humidity, X-ray dose and crystal size.
nodes.loc: Introduction, last paragraph; Results: 'Experimental factors leading to high data quality and reproducibility'

nodes.title: QUE - How does X-ray dose change the diffuse signal?
nodes.desc: Radiation damage is a possible source of correlated disorder, but how it shows up in diffuse scattering was unclear.

nodes.title: CLM - Diffuse maps from the East (CHESS) and West (ALS) teams agree within experimental error
nodes.desc: Agreement between the two teams was comparable to agreement between repeated visits by one team.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Comparing data quality and consistency across datasets'; Discussion, paragraph 1

nodes.title: CLM - Diffuse maps are reproducible across repeated synchrotron visits by the same team
nodes.desc: Each team collected two independent multi-crystal datasets on different visits, and each pair agreed within noise above about 6 Å.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Four high-quality datasets establish a baseline for reproducibility'; Discussion, paragraph 1

nodes.title: CLM - mdx2 processing gives consistent diffuse maps across different detectors and beamlines
nodes.desc: Data from an Eiger2 X 16M (CHESS) and a Pilatus3 S 6M (ALS), in different image formats, produced visually similar maps.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Separating isotropic and anisotropic contributions', paragraph 1, Figure 1

nodes.title: CLM - The Mac1 maps match the quality of earlier lysozyme datasets, so the GOODVIBES/DISCOBALL workflow can be applied
nodes.desc: The maps show the same feature types (halos, cloudy patterns) and set a baseline for perturbation experiments such as ligand binding or temperature.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Comparing data quality and consistency across datasets', last paragraph

nodes.title: CLM - The isotropic and anisotropic diffuse components likely have different physical origins
nodes.desc: Their resolution profiles are similar in shape, but the peaks do not sit at the same resolution.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Separating isotropic and anisotropic contributions', last paragraph, Figure 2a

nodes.title: CLM - CC_lim, the product of two datasets' CC* values, is the maximum correlation expected from noise alone
nodes.desc: If the pairwise map correlation (CC_pair) falls below CC_lim in a resolution shell, the two maps differ beyond noise in that shell.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Comparing data quality and consistency across datasets'; Methods: 'Derivation of CC_lim'

nodes.title: CLM - Humidity-controlled Mac1 crystals from one team are highly isomorphous with very low mosaicity
nodes.desc: Low mosaicity indicates no dehydration stress during mounting and lets diffuse scattering be measured close to Bragg peaks.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Four high-quality datasets establish a baseline for reproducibility', Table 1

nodes.title: CLM - Merging crystals in diverse orientations improves reciprocal-space coverage and diffuse signal-to-noise
nodes.desc: Mac1 crystals sit on the loop in a preferred orientation. Sampling diverse orientations matters more than reaching a strict minimum number of crystals.

nodes.title: CLM - Mac1 crystals need humidity control and a sleeve mount; oil coating offers little benefit
nodes.desc: Oil coating can compromise both crystal hydration and lattice order. Only a sleeve without oil matched the humidity-controlled references.

nodes.title: CLM - Sleeve mounts allow a matched background measurement; oil mounts do not
nodes.desc: Translating along the sleeve gives an equivalent path length of the same material. Oil around the crystal varies between mounts and with rotation.

nodes.title: CLM - Larger crystals are the most direct route to a stronger reproducible diffuse signal
nodes.desc: Dose limits rule out more flux or longer exposures, so a larger illuminated volume is the remaining way to boost signal for a given dose.

nodes.title: CLM - Radiation damage leaves a measurable signature in the diffuse signal
nodes.desc: This gives a diagnostic for dose effects when screening data. The authors also identify a low-dose regime where damage is negligible relative to other errors.

nodes.title: CLM - Global radiation damage acts as a resolution-dependent rescaling of the anisotropic pattern
nodes.desc: The simplest elastic-lattice model: dose raises the effective temperature or lowers stiffness, which in the one-phonon approximation rescales the pattern as B rises. The paper's data go against this.

nodes.title: CLM - Radiation damage may be concentrated in microscopic regions or defects of the crystal
nodes.desc: Offered as one possible explanation, consistent with 4D-STEM images of nanoscale domain reorientation in lysozyme and myoglobin crystals. Not tested here.

nodes.title: EVD - The four diffuse maps look nearly identical: halos in integer planes, cloudy patterns in half-integer planes to 1.25 Å
nodes.desc: Maps were reconstructed on a 2x2x4 oversampled grid and normalized to the isotropic maximum. Total intensity shows a bright ring at about 3.3 Å.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Separating isotropic and anisotropic contributions', Figure 1

nodes.title: EVD - Isotropic profiles match across datasets: peak at ~3.3 Å, shoulder at ~2.2 Å, flat beyond 1.7 Å
nodes.desc: The anisotropic RMS profile and its overall magnitude are also consistent between the four datasets.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Separating isotropic and anisotropic contributions', Figure 2a

nodes.title: EVD - CC_pair closely approaches CC_lim for all six dataset pairs, with gaps only below ~6 Å
nodes.desc: The low-resolution gaps appear within teams (ALS vs ALS, CHESS vs CHESS) as well, so they are not site effects. No significant East vs West differences.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Comparing data quality and consistency across datasets', Figure 2b

nodes.title: EVD - CC* exceeds 0.85 from 6 to 2.2 Å and reaches 0.965-0.997 near 4 Å in all four datasets
nodes.desc: CHESS 2025-11-05, from two crystals about 500 µm across, has the highest signal-to-noise and keeps CC* above 0.95 from 13.3 to 1.8 Å.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Assessing internal data quality of individual datasets', Figure 2b

nodes.title: EVD - The main anisotropic peak sits at lower resolution than the 3.3 Å isotropic peak
nodes.desc: Both signals are small at low resolution, peak in the water ring, show a shoulder and decay at high resolution, but the peak positions differ.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Separating isotropic and anisotropic contributions', last paragraph, Figure 2a

nodes.title: EVD - Low-dose halves: CC_pair matches CC_lim at all resolutions; high-dose halves fall below CC_lim from 10 to 5 Å
nodes.desc: The high-dose gap closes around 2.5 Å and beyond. CC_lim here is the product of the two halves' CC* values.

nodes.title: EVD - Bragg resolution regularly exceeds 1.1 Å, DIALS mosaicity is 0.014° or lower, and merged completeness is 100%
nodes.desc: Resolution is on par with the best room-temperature P4_3 Mac1 structures (e.g. 7TWF). Data were truncated at 1.25 Å for all datasets; single crystals had lower outer-shell completeness.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Four high-quality datasets establish a baseline for reproducibility', Table 1

nodes.title: EVD - Outer-shell CC1/2 rises after merging in every dataset, e.g. 0.871, 0.942, 0.929 to 0.980 (ALS 2025-10-15)
nodes.desc: CHESS 2025-11-05 rose from 0.988 and 0.984 to 0.994. An increase is expected only if the crystals are truly isomorphous.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Four high-quality datasets establish a baseline for reproducibility', Table 1

nodes.title: EVD - Unit cells are consistent within each team; ALS crystals have ~2.5% larger volume than CHESS crystals
nodes.desc: ALS a = 89.22-89.27 Å, CHESS a = 88.41-88.44 Å. The authors attribute the between-team difference to crystallization (sitting vs hanging drop).
nodes.loc: Results: 'Four high-quality datasets establish a baseline for reproducibility', Table 1

nodes.title: EVD - Single-crystal maps show a propeller pattern that fades in two-crystal merges and is absent with three crystals
nodes.desc: The pattern comes from uneven multiplicity and stays visible for xtal2 + xtal3, which had similar orientations.

nodes.title: EVD - Signal reaches noise at 1.8-2 Å for single crystals and at 1.6 Å for the three-crystal merge
nodes.desc: Signal-to-noise is the noise-corrected anisotropic RMS intensity over the RMS propagated error, and rises with each added crystal.

nodes.title: EVD - Paratone-N without a sleeve: Wilson B 20.5 vs 13.1 Å², mosaicity 0.120° vs 0.014°, c 39.48 vs 40.20 Å
nodes.desc: Every Bragg quality indicator was worse than the humidity-controlled references, consistent with dehydration during mounting.

nodes.title: EVD - Sleeve plus oil: Wilson B back to 11.7-12.6 Å², but c is ~0.5 Å short and Santovac-5 mosaicity is 0.186°
nodes.desc: With Paratone-N in a sleeve, mosaicity was 0.022°. The shorter c axes suggest partial dehydration even inside a sleeve.

nodes.title: EVD - Sleeve without oil: mosaicity 0.009° and both unit cell axes within ~0.1 Å of the references
nodes.desc: It was the only ambient-harvested mount that matched the references on all four metrics.

nodes.title: EVD - Background collected 100-300 µm from the crystal on the sleeve matched well; background at the Kapton loop neck did not
nodes.desc: The loop-neck background likely led to oversubtraction.

nodes.title: EVD - Small crystals (~100 µm) have 4- to 5-fold lower signal-to-noise and reach noise at ~2.1 Å vs ~1.25 Å
nodes.desc: This holds even though the small-crystal merge has three crystals and the large-crystal merge (CHESS 2025-11-05) only two.

nodes.title: EVD - Small-crystal maps show the same principal features but are weaker and less sharply defined
nodes.desc: The isotropic profile is lower near the 2.2-2.5 Å shoulder. Part of the difference may come from scaling and merging noisier data.

nodes.title: EVD - Doubling exposure per frame raised mosaicity from 0.014° to 0.056° and Wilson B from 13.2 to 13.9 Å²
nodes.desc: 0.1 s vs 0.05 s per 0.1° frame at ALS, with humidity-controlled harvesting, so the comparison isolates X-ray dose.

nodes.title: EVD - High-dose diffuse changes sit mostly at low resolution and the pattern changes shape rather than rescaling
nodes.desc: The second high-dose half has higher RMS intensity near 10 Å and stronger features at d > ~4 Å. The low-dose halves look nearly identical.

nodes.title: STU - Four high-quality multi-crystal Mac1 datasets, two per team
nodes.desc: East: CHESS ID7B2, 2025-09-24 (3 crystals) and 2025-11-05 (2). West: ALS 8.3.1, 2025-10-15 (3) and 2025-11-25 (2). Also SBGrid Databank 1301 to 1304.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Optimized data collection procedure'; 'Four high-quality datasets'; Table 1

nodes.title: STU - Resolution-shell comparison of the four anisotropic diffuse maps
nodes.desc: Isotropic and anisotropic profiles, CC* per dataset, and CC_pair against CC_lim for every pair.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Assessing internal data quality'; 'Comparing data quality and consistency across datasets', Figure 2

nodes.title: STU - Crystal-number analysis: every one-, two- and three-crystal merge of CHESS 2025-09-24
nodes.desc: Compares reciprocal-space uniformity and signal-to-noise as crystals are added.

nodes.title: STU - Mounting-condition test at ALS 2025-07-01 without humidity control
nodes.desc: Four single-crystal conditions (oil type and sleeve) compared by Bragg statistics against two humidity-controlled ALS references. Diffuse maps were not extracted.

nodes.title: STU - X-ray dose test at ALS: high-dose single crystal vs the ALS 2025-10-15 reference
nodes.desc: Each rotation series was split at its midpoint and the halves merged with a common scale model.

nodes.title: STU - Crystal-size test: ALS 2026-04-23 small crystals vs CHESS 2025-11-05 large crystals
nodes.desc: Three ~100 µm crystals vs two 200-400 µm crystals, both humidity controlled and at matched low dose.

nodes.title: PRO - Mac1 expression, purification and seeded crystallization at UCSF and Cornell
nodes.desc: P4_3 Mac1 (residues 3-169) from E. coli, His-tag cleaved, 40 mg/mL. Sitting drops at UCSF and hanging drops at Cornell over 100 mM CHES pH 9.5 with PEG 3000; PEG and seed dilution tune crystal size.

nodes.title: PRO - Humidity-controlled harvesting into plastic capillaries
nodes.desc: Harvested in a MiTeGen SLEEC chamber (~100% RH) or humidified gas stream (~90% RH), with Kapton loops in MicroRT capillaries and well solution 2-4 mm from the crystal.
nodes.loc: Results: 'Optimized data collection procedure'; Methods: 'Data collection'

nodes.title: PRO - Low-dose room-temperature diffuse data collection with matched background
nodes.desc: ~100 µm beam, about 10^11 photons/s, shutterless 0.1° frames over ~720°. A 360° background is taken 100-300 µm along the spindle at the same fluence per degree. Datasets are truncated until B decay is below 2 Å².
nodes.loc: Results: 'Optimized data collection procedure'; Methods: 'Data collection'

nodes.title: PRO - DIALS Bragg processing then mdx2 diffuse integration, scaling and merging
nodes.desc: 2x2x4 oversampled grid, background correction, joint scaling, symmetry averaging. The isotropic part is a trimmed mean in 0.01 Å⁻¹ shells and is subtracted to give the anisotropic map.

nodes.title: PRO - CC1/2, CC* and CC_lim statistics on anisotropic maps per resolution shell
nodes.desc: Random half-datasets give CC1/2 and CC*. CC_lim is the product of two datasets' CC*. All CCs use the anisotropic pattern because the isotropic part inflates them.

nodes.title: REQ - Build diffuse maps from larger numbers of crystals
nodes.desc: To find how signal quality keeps improving as more datasets are merged.

nodes.title: REQ - Determine how diffuse signal-to-noise propagates into the models derived from the maps
nodes.desc: This will set the crystal size and signal strength needed for a given interpretive claim, including whether ~100 µm crystals are enough.

nodes.title: REQ - Establish the mechanism of dose-dependent diffuse changes across systems beyond Mac1
nodes.desc: Different crystals may respond differently to X-ray dose, so the effects need systematic study.
nodes.loc: Results: 'X-ray Dose', last paragraph; Discussion, paragraph 3

nodes.title: REQ - Run Mac1 perturbation experiments (ligand binding, temperature) against this baseline
nodes.desc: Several perturbation datasets are already collected (see the online logbooks).

nodes.title: REQ - Separate lattice from internal motion with GOODVIBES and 3D-ΔPDF, and test dynamics models against the maps
nodes.desc: Testing models of protein dynamics directly against diffuse data is a long-term goal of the sampleworks project.
